title: South Koreans Are Eating Less Kimchi
paragraphs: Kimchi, a spicy dish made from fermented vegetables, is famous around the world as a symbol of Korean food. However, according to a new study, fewer South Koreans are eating it every day.

The study was carried out by researchers from Chung-Ang University, Jeju National University and the World Institute of Kimchi. They used data from a national health and nutrition survey in South Korea between 2010 and 2024.

The researchers found that the share of people who had not eaten any kimchi in the previous 24 hours almost doubled during that time. In 2010, the figure was 11.7%, but by 2024, it had risen to 22.7%. The change was seen in both men and women. Among men, the share rose from 10.2% to 20.6%, and among women, it rose from 13.1% to 24.8%.

Fewer people are also eating kimchi as a side dish. This was true for every age group except children under 10. The biggest drop was among people aged 20 to 39. In this group, the share eating kimchi as a side dish fell from 82% to 66%. However, more people are now using kimchi as an ingredient in cooked dishes, such as kimchi stew.

Why is this happening? The researchers say that it reflects wider changes in the way Koreans eat. For example, there are more people living alone, and more people are eating ready-made meals and eating out. In addition, fewer people are eating traditional meals of rice, soup and side dishes.
Interestingly, the researchers do not think the government should simply encourage people to eat more kimchi. Instead, they believe it should encourage people to eat more balanced diets.
At the same time, kimchi is becoming more and more popular in other countries.
